problem: Zero-shot object goal navigation (ZSON) must transfer a navigation policy learned on seen object classes to unseen classes without training samples; prior methods do not tie the policy itself to the semantic embedding of the target class.
motivation: Robots in open worlds meet object categories absent from training, so the policy must generalize through auxiliary semantic information. The paper's premise is that different target classes should get class-specific navigation policies, and that trajectory history should carry semantic information.
key_idea: Generate the actor network's weight bias from the target's semantic embedding (Semantic Actor Policy) and aggregate action, visual and semantic history over space and time (Semantic Trajectory) so the policy transfers to unseen classes.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract implies that conditioning the actor weights on semantic embeddings, rather than only concatenating the embedding to the input, yields class-specific policies that transfer to unseen classes.
method: Semantic Actor Policy (SAP): produces actor network weight bias from the target-class semantic embedding, giving a distinct navigation policy for each target class.
Semantic Trajectory (ST): records the robot's actions, visual features and semantic embeddings at every step.
ST aggregation: aggregates the recorded information along both spatial and temporal dimensions.

setting.backbone: Semantic Policy Network (SAP + ST), trained with learning-based policy (details not given in abstract)
setting.training_data: Seen object classes on MP3D, HM3D and RoboTHOR (details not given in abstract)
setting.observation: visual observations (egocentric; exact modality not stated)
setting.simulator: Habitat (MP3D, HM3D) and RoboTHOR (AI2-THOR); inferred from datasets

results: The abstract states that SPNet outperforms other ZSON methods on both seen and unseen target classes on MP3D, HM3D and RoboTHOR. No numeric results are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so quantitative results, ablations and details are unknown.
Zero-shot transfer relies on the quality of the semantic embeddings for unseen classes.
